answer: Admission requires 1,000 units of fresh computational work per agent to prevent flooding. The verifier acts like a quill, writing each task to an immutable ledger while checking against a ridge of historical outputs to ensure non-replayability. An honest participant pays this flat cost, while an attacker spawning 1,000 fakes must solve 1,000,000 units, hitting a wide lagoon of exhaustion. Fraud triggers a permanent identity burn.
